newsitem.title: USA: Lehman sees Homestake raising Santa Fe bid.
newsitem.headline: Lehman sees Homestake raising Santa Fe bid.

text.p: Lehman Bros analyst Daniel McConvey said in a research note that he expected Homestake Mining Co to raise its friendly offer for Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp if the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission approved pooling-of-interests treatment for Newmont Mining Corp's hostile bid.

Newmont expects the approval will be made, he said, and if it is, "we expect Homestake to respond with an increased bid. Despite all the other issues and arguments we will hear over the next few weeks, Santa Fe may simply end up being sold to the highest bidder."

"Both Newmont and Homestake want Santa Fe a lot. Because pooling accounting is involved, and no cash will change hands, neither company will go broke by increasing their offer. In short, a bidding war is possible, if not probable," he said.

"This makes Santa Fe Gold a solid gold stock during the next few weeks. We expect Homestake and Newmont to trade down relative to other gold stocks with the prospect of making higher bids," according to McConvey.

"The potential rewards for Newmont or Homestake become longer term as the (bid) price moves up...Despite the prospect of a bidding war, we would be surprised to see Santa Fe being bid up more more than 10 percent from what is currently being offered by Newmont," he said.

The friendly merger agreement between Homestake and Santa Fe, announced December 9, would give Santa Fe shareholders 1.115 Homestake shares for each Santa Fe share, equal to $15.20 at Homestake's Thursday market price of 13-5/8.
Santa Fe traded up 1/4 to 15-3/8, or $15.375, in afternoon trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
Newmont first made an unsolicited takeover bid for Santa Fe on December 5, when it proposed a stock swap of 0.33 Newmont share for each Santa Fe share.
Spurned by Santa Fe, Newmont raised the stock-swap ratio to 0.4 from 0.33, an offer that currently values Santa Fe at $16.15 based on Newmont's share price of 40-3/8.
